course: I find that the criteria in which our blogs are assessed are inconsistent and unclear. The guidelines about how to write blogs the way they want us to do were not clear cut. It was stated that our blogs are a result of our creative process and they should be personal but when the blogs did not fit to the courses or the lecturers understanding of “personal” we lost points and on top of that there also was some ambiguous restrictions on what you could write and what you couldn't write on a creative blog, for example they deducted points for writing suggestions or anything close to one,   so in a lot of instances our creative directions were not understood or respected. If it is our creative process I do not understand why our blogs were graded with subjective standards. I do not think any outside authority can decide what is and what is not personal for me, I am the only one who knows my own inner workings as the individual themselves. I do not have to write my childhood memories for something to be personal, if I identify more with a philosophical approach/conveying my inner thoughts and understandings about the subject in a deep manner that does not make it generalized or not personal it shows the way in which I process the world. To summarize my feedback: I feel our creative processes and individuality were not respected and if they want us to write the blogs in very specific ways there should be clear templates that are communicated but I would prefer creative freedom rather than uninspiring guidelines.
